### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**46** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4abed176b7ad68cdbd7c7e9b94705b5a013c61e8` — the merge of head `b012326f35cb828c16c6bb0907062cfc374dbdbc` into base `d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4abed176b7ad68cdbd7c7e9b94705b5a013c61e8 && git checkout 4abed176b7ad68cdbd7c7e9b94705b5a013c61e8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef b012326f35cb828c16c6bb0907062cfc374dbdbc && git checkout -B drift-repro d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef && git merge --no-ff b012326f35cb828c16c6bb0907062cfc374dbdbc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d3f3f4abf9f392a49fecf77f2175424fe1680bef` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b012326f35cb828c16c6bb0907062cfc374dbdbc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts

Inputs read: card #33250 body and all six comments (triage 6880118668, hold 6880158095, analysis 6880272329, ruling record 6880588685, claim 6880627606, dev report 6881619847); PR #33369 body, its 40-file list and the net diff against merge-base `24f2f401`; check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read on the head tree, not reviewed (step 2.7 and 2.8 in `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `readRowById`, `readUnlessRefused`, `assertMasterRowEditable`, the attachment and comment gates).

Check-runs at render (69 total): 29 success, 11 skipped, 29 still in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green: Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint and Repo Gates and all Lint shards, PM dispatch-gates, Type Check source gates and debt ledger, Build Docs, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI. No conclusion yet: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build Core, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI. This verdict is the design judgment; those runs are the test verdicts and the seat reads them before enqueue.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Accept-set of `ObjectSchema`: one new optional boolean, `sharing.controlledByParent.writeRequiresMasterRead`, inside the strict sub-object. Widening. Right.
2. Two parse refusals, both on declarations that did not parse on `main` (the key was unknown): `true` off a `controlled_by_parent` object, at `sharing.controlledByParent.writeRequiresMasterRead`; `true` beside `ownerMayEdit: true`, at `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit`. Neither narrows anything `main` accepted. `false` is accepted everywhere, as the sibling key is. Right.
3. New public export `controlledByParentWriteRequiresMasterRead` from `@objectstack/spec/data` (api-surface and export-origins rows present). Right.
4. `ISecurityService`: prose only. `ControlledByParentWriteDenialLeg` is not widened; a refused read maps to `object_permission`, an unreadable master row to `row_level_security`, and the jsdoc says `record_sharing` is never the leg of a read hop. An exhaustive consumer switch is unaffected. Right (see ③ for the dev's flag).
5. Runtime answers move toward admit only for a write whose chain reaches a hop that declares the key. That includes one case the summary sentences do not name: a detail that does NOT declare the key, under a `controlled_by_parent` master that does (`omd_line` under `omd_milestone` in the tests). It asks the edit legs on its master, then that master's own hop asks read, so it is written by someone who cannot edit the top master. Judged right: the walk has always asked "may this principal edit the master", and the master's declaration now defines that; the master's object-level update grant and its authored update policies still run on that hop (`assertMasterRowEditable`, floor handed over exactly as step 2.7 does for the master's own by-id write). It is named here because it is the one place "an object that does not declare the key is unchanged" is not literally true (finding N1).
6. The swap is verb-blind: the gate runs for `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `transfer`, `restore` and `purge` (step 2.8), so on an opted-in detail the lifecycle verbs ask read too. Consistent with the gate's one-question-for-every-verb rule and with the schema text "every write"; the detail's own grants for those verbs still decide. Right.
7. Lint: `security-controlled-by-parent-owner-policy-without-opt-in` stands down, both branches, on a detail that declares the key. Fewer warnings, no new rule. Right: on such a detail a caller-keyed update policy decides among master readers as authored, whichever field it keys.
8. A stack in which no object declares the key takes no new branch: `hopRel.writeRequiresMasterRead` is `false` on every hop, refusal sentences keep "requires edit access", the `MASTER_DENIAL_QUESTION` map is never written. Acceptance 3 holds.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/33250-controlled-by-parent-write-requires-master-read.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor (new authorable key, new export), `@objectstack/plugin-security` minor (new admitted behaviour), `@objectstack/lint` patch (an existing rule stands down, no rule added), `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch and `@object-ui/app-shell` patch (labels). Matches what the diff publishes. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

Clause-②: yes (widening), on the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: added`. Correct: the accept-set grows by one key and the two refusals fall only on declarations that carry the new key.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, by-id update or delete without master read answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, not the card's "403": accepted. Read in the tree: step 2.7 (`callerCannotReadAddressedRow`) runs before step 2.8, and a detail row's read derives from its master, so the row is hidden before the gate is reached. That is the hidden-row rule (#7505) and `main` answers the same for a non-opted detail; answering 403 would tell a caller who cannot read the row that it exists. Acceptance 2's intent (the write is refused) holds; insert and re-point answer `403` asking read; the served member answers `deny` for all of them. The card's wording was loose, the code is right.
- Dev deviation, PR body Verification section mangled at create: the body on the head now reads whole and carries the seat's signature. Closed.
- Dev flag, denial legs reused rather than widening the closed union: confirmed, see ① item 4.
- Dev flag and analysis gap 3, on-behalf-of: confirmed against ADR-0090 D10 rule 1 (intersection, never union). Step 2.8 calls the gate once with the agent's context and once with the delegator's, and each pass asks the read door under its own context; either one unable to read refuses. The delegated by-id path also keeps both platform floors, as before. An agent never exceeds its delegator. The 2026-10-26 amendment kept delegation out of the owner leg because that relief is keyed on one identity; this one is not.
- Ruling coverage: ruling record 6880588685 (A+, Leehom, 2026-11-14T16:21:29Z) rules insert, update and delete by opt-in, default unchanged, and lifts the "Option 2 was not chosen" line of `6398566164` for opted-in objects. Key name, covered paths, relation to `ownerMayEdit` and the lint arm were left to the seat; ① items 5 and 6 are the two seat calls the veto window should see.
- `open_questions`: none filed.
- Owed at landing, not in this diff by the claim's own bar (`docs/adr/**` and `skills/**` are carriers): the ADR-0055 amendment and the `skills/**` teaching (acceptance 5's second half; PR body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up owed`). The code, the schema `.describe()` and the jsdoc already cite "ADR-0055 §3 as amended for #33250", and ADR-0055 on `main` still says "Option 2's door stays closed". The PR says `Fixes #33250`, so the card closes on merge: the seat files both carriers at landing, as the ruling record says, so the ADR does not stay narrower than the runtime (the hazard ADR-0055's own chain amendment describes).

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`** — holds. The key sits in the strict `controlledByParent` block; the reader is fail-closed (`=== true` only) and does not read `sharingModel`, the same shape as its sibling. The refusal runs in the same `superRefine` as the sibling's. Both messages name the fix. The pair refusal is sound: with read as the master question for every principal, the owner leg admits no one more; at a door that does not parse, both keys together behave as the wider one, so nothing depends on the refusal for safety. The `sharing` guidance map gains the misplacement hint. The `.describe()` and jsdoc agree with the gate hop by hop.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`** — holds. Each added sentence was checked against the gate: read in place of the three edit legs on a declaring hop and the walk ends there (`assertControlledByParentChainEditable`, the `break` after `assertMasterRowReadable`); `object_permission` on a refused read, `row_level_security` on a row not returned (`readUnlessRefused`); agent then delegator (`checkControlledByParentWrite`, same two calls as step 2.8). The existing sentence "It answers the master check alone" matters more now: for an opted-in detail `allow` means "reads the master", so a consumer must still compose the record's own grants. The shipped attachment and comment gates do (they ask `explain`'s record-grained update verdict and use this member only where no `explain` is served).

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts`** — holds. One boolean toggle in the existing block; help text states the default, the effect and the pair rule.

**`security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, `security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts`, `security-plugin.ts`** — the code agrees with the contract. Attempts to break it:

- Widening without opt-in: none in a stack that does not declare the key. The one cross-object effect is ① item 5, judged right.
- Chain hops: an opted detail under a non-opted `controlled_by_parent` master asks read on that master and stops; the read door composes the chain above (ADR-0139 D6), so a hidden top master hides the middle one and refuses (pinned: `omd_step`, blind caller, `row_level_security`). Cycle and depth guards are not bypassed in a way that matters: the read hop terminates the walk and the read derivation carries its own bound.
- Re-point and emptying: the stored master and the body-named master are both asked through the same walk, so both get the detail's question. A master reader can move a row between two masters they read, or detach it from an optional master; each is no more than the delete plus insert the ruling already admits.
- Predicate writes: every master of the selected rows is asked through the walk; the platform ownership floor on the detail stays for predicate writes, as on `main`.
- Delegation: see ③.
- The read probe: `readRowById(master, id, context)` is `ql.findOne` under the principal's own context, the same probe the owner leg has used since #26005; a declared 4xx is a refusal, a null row is hidden-or-absent (one answer), a store fault propagates. No system-context read decides access (the two system reads only fetch a foreign key, as before).
- Refusal wording: the question (`edit` or `read`) travels beside the error in a weak map, so the envelope is unchanged and a caller who cannot read the master reference still gets the generic sentence, now with the right verb.

**`explain-engine.ts`** — agrees. The verdict still comes from `checkControlledByParentWrite`; `chainAsksMasterRead` only chooses prose, and the prose it chooses states both questions a leg can answer.

**`validate-security-posture.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`** — agree. The stand-down reads the key through the spec's one reader, raw or parsed.

Findings:

- **N1 — nit.** Three summary sentences say an object that does not declare the key is unchanged "byte for byte": the gate's file header ("A detail that does not declare it is answered byte for byte as before"), the PR body's Clause-② line and the changeset's first paragraph. Not literally true for a non-declaring detail under a declaring `controlled_by_parent` master (① item 5). The precise invariant is: a write's answer moves only if its own object, or a `controlled_by_parent` master on its chain, declares the key. The contract text itself (schema jsdoc, `.describe()`, the changeset's hop bullet) states the hop rule correctly, so nothing a consumer relies on is wrong. Fix on the PR body sentence, or carry the wording into the ADR-0055 amendment; leave the code comment as an accepted deviation.
- **N2 — nit.** Comments in the gate that predate the key still say unconditionally that a body which empties an optional master, or names a new one, "asks EDIT" (the `askBodyNamedMaster` docblock and the fifth owner-leg condition). On an opted-in detail it asks read, as the new header says. Comment drift only; follow-up.
- **N3 — nit.** `.describe()` says a write on behalf of another user is admitted "when both can read the master". A delegated by-id update or delete also keeps both platform ownership floors (pre-existing D10 exclusion, pinned in the new delegated-update test), and a predicate write keeps the floor too. The sentence is covered by "as the detail's own ... row-level security ... allow" only if the reader knows the floor is a platform policy. The ADR amendment and the skill should say it in plain words.
- **N4 — nit, follow-up pins.** Two shapes are covered by construction and not pinned under the opt-in: an update that empties an optional master, and the lifecycle verbs (`transfer`, `restore`, `purge`). Tests are the lane seat's accept; named here because the PR body lists emptying among the covered paths.
- **Observation, outside the diff (read, not reviewed).** The fallback branch of the attachment and comment gates (a security service that serves `checkControlledByParentWrite` but no `explain`) admits on `allow` alone. The shipped `SecurityPlugin` always serves `explain`, so the branch is not reached in a shipped kernel; with a third-party security service and an opted-in detail it would admit any master reader. Worth one line in the carrier that documents the member.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## ACCEPT · PR #33369 (#33250, p1) · head `b012326f35cb828c16c6bb0907062cfc374dbdbc` · 2026-11-14T18:13Z

## 席位核对

- **形态:** 40 files, +1006/−47 (read with `get_files`, not the report): the key `sharing.controlledByParent.writeRequiresMasterRead`, its reader and two parse refusals in `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` / `object.form.ts`; prose on `ISecurityService` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`); the per-hop read branch in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts`, relation resolution, `explain-engine.ts`; the lint stand-down; i18n bundles, generated references, hand-written pages; tests; changesets (spec and plugin-security minor; lint, platform-objects, app-shell patch). No governed path (`docs/adr/**` and `skills/**` are carried by cards), under 3000 lines: Tier S, seat lands. PR body rewritten by the seat (the dev's `## Verification` was mangled at create; same head).
- **前提实测:** the ruling this implements is Leehom's A+ 「开关打开后,能读主记录的人按子对象自己的授权新增、修改、删除,默认不变。」 (2026-11-14T16:21:29Z, ruling record 6880588685). Key name, covered paths, relation to `ownerMayEdit` and the lint arm were the seat's to set (record 6880588685).
- **门禁 check-runs:** on this head 72 runs: 61 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed. Dev's NOT-MEASURED `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is answered by CI.
- **契约复审:** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` PASS on this head, record 6881744779 (isolated reviewer; Ruling-ref 「你有 fable ，车道契约复审可以自己做」 2026-11-07). Four nits, no must-fix or should-fix. The two seat calls the record names (① 5: a non-opted detail under an opted master is writable by a reader of the top master, the master's own update grant and policies still running on its hop; ① 6: lifecycle verbs ask read on an opted detail) are inside the ruling's "增改删 by the detail's own grants" and are accepted; they are written into the ADR-0055 amendment card.
- **接受的偏差:** the dev's 404-vs-403 deviation (a by-id update/delete by a non-reader answers `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` because the read door runs first, #7505, as on `main`; insert and re-point answer 403); N1 wording "byte for byte" left in the code comment and changeset. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added` on PR body and changesets.
- **范围外去向:** ADR-0055 amendment — card #33373 (`domain:skills`, p2, Tier H; N1 and N3 wording added); `skills/**` guidance (`Skills-docs: follow-up owed`) — card #33374 (`domain:skills`, p2, Tier H); N2 stale "asks EDIT" comments and N4 missing pins (emptying a master, lifecycle verbs) — card #33381 (`domain:server`, p3). Reviewer's observation on the attachment/comment gates' fallback branch — dropped — unreachable in a shipped kernel (`SecurityPlugin` always serves `explain`), read not reviewed.
- **落地条款:** ready + auto-merge now under the maintainer's standing order 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z). K = 7 commits on `main` past the run's affected-set base `d3f3f4ab`, below 15: no merge of main owed.
